sections.html: Hyphessobrycon peugeotorum is a beautiful tetra. The species grows to a length of 4-5 cm and is completely peaceful.

Hyphessobrycon peugeotorum was only scientifically described in 2013 under the name H. peugeoti. It originates from the Brazilian state of Mato Grosso (middle drainage of the Rio Juruena, upper basin of the Rio Tapajós).

The unusual species name does not refer to the French car builders, but (quotation): “Hyphessobrycon peugeoti is patronymic to the Peugeot family, who invented the Peugeot pepper mill mechanism in 1842 and whose manufacturing business led to the establishment of a carbon sink reforestation project in the fazenda São Nicolau, in central Brazil, and eventually to the discovery of this new species.” According to the rules of zoological naming, in this case (naming after several individuals, not after a single individual) the Latin plural genitive must be chosen for the species name – i.e. the word ending -orum – and not, as happened, the Latin singular genitive ending in -i.

An objection was raised against the change of the species name peugeoti to peugeotorum, so the species is currently more frequently referred to as H. peugeoti again.

An experience in the photo tank indicates how the animal should be cared for in order to achieve optimum coloration. In the fishhouse, a male showed mating coloration and developed a black caudal fin (in normal coloration, the caudal fin is transparent and colorless). The animal and some conspecifics were caught and put in the photo tank. It shouldn’t normally take long for the now decolored animal to show mating colors again. Not so! Nine days passed and nothing happened. The water was warmed, humic substances were added, live food was fed, water was changed – everything you do to get tetras going. Nothing. Then the tank was darkened considerably, and that worked. Apparently Hyphessobrycon peugeotorum likes it a bit dim.
